answers.question: Why does the billing module have a cash point concept? Explain what it is used for and where it appears in code.

paragraphs.text: A **cash point** is the physical till or cashier station where money is taken and bills are settled — for example "Pharmacy Cash Point" or "Main Cash Point". It exists so that the billing system knows *where* a bill was created and paid, not just *who* took the money. Bills and cashier timesheets both point at a cash point, which lets an administrator reconcile cash per station and generate receipt numbers that are grouped by station.
Here is how it fits together.

`CashPoint` is a small metadata entity (a catalogue entry, like a location or a concept) with a name, a description, a retired flag and — importantly — an associated OpenMRS `Location` [1]. The class comment states its purpose plainly: "a location where Bills can be created and paid for" [2]. Because a point belongs to a location, a hospital with several sites can have separate tills per site, and queries like "all cash points at this location" are cheap.

1. **Attribution of a bill to a till.** Every `Bill` carries a mandatory `cashPoint` field [3], and the Hibernate mapping makes it `not-null` in the database [4]. So the system cannot record a bill without knowing the station that produced it.

2. **Tracking cashier shifts.** A `Timesheet` records when a cashier clocked in and out at a given cash point: it has a `cashier` (a provider), a `cashPoint`, `clockIn` and `clockOut` [5]. When a legacy cashier page opens and there is no open timesheet, the controller creates a new one and sets the cashier and clock-in time [6], offering the available cash points through the `cashPoints` model attribute [7].

3. **Receipt numbering.** Receipt numbers can be grouped by cash point. The generator's `GroupingType` enum includes `CASH_POINT` and `CASHIER_AND_CASH_POINT` [8], and `createGrouping` builds the prefix from the bill's cash point id [9]. The prefix text is configurable and defaults to `"CP"` [10].
## Where it appears in the module

| Layer | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `CashPoint` [11] | The entity (name, description, location, retired) |
| Model | `Bill.cashPoint` [3] | Every bill belongs to a till |
| Model | `Timesheet.cashPoint` [12] | Every shift belongs to a till |
| Service | `CashPointService` / `CashPointServiceImpl` [13] | CRUD plus lookups by location, name and retired flag |
| Search | `CashPointSearch` [14] | Filter by location UUID, name or include retired |
| DAO | `HibernateCashPointDAOImpl.getCashPoints` [15] | Builds the criteria query |
| REST | `CashPointResource` [16] | Exposes `/ws/rest/v1/billing/cashPoint` |
| Tables | `cashier_cash_point` [17], foreign keys into `cashier_bill` and `cashier_timesheet` [18] | Persistence and referential integrity |

Service lookups are also exposed by location: `getCashPointsByLocation` requires a location and rejects a null one [19], and `getCashPointsByLocationAndName` additionally validates the name and caps it at 255 characters [20].
## How a cash point gets onto a bill
There are two paths, and this is the interesting part.

**Path A — automatic billing from a clinical order.** When a doctor's order is turned into a bill, the strategy pattern is used: `OrderBillingStrategy` declares `resolveCashPoint()` [21], the base class returns `null` by default [22], and the concrete drug and test strategies simply pick the first non-retired cash point [23] [24]. `createBill` then requires a non-null cash point, and if none can be resolved it logs an error and skips billing entirely [25]. This is exactly why the concept exists: without a till there is nowhere to attribute the charge, so the module refuses to create the bill rather than create an unattributable one. Note that these strategies currently just take the first cash point — a placeholder that assumes a single-till deployment.

**Path B — the O3 frontend.** In `openmrs-esm-billing-app`, a "Cash point configuration" admin page is registered in the billing settings menu [26], backed by a list component that fetches `/billing/cashPoint?v=full` [27] and an "Add Cash Point" modal that posts name, UUID and location to the same endpoint [28]. There is also a default cash point UUID in the module's config schema, described as "the cashier station/location where bills are processed" [29]. At checkout, `useCashPoint()` fetches the list [30], and the check-in form attaches the first cash point's UUID to the bill payload that it POSTs to `/bill` [31]. Bills read back from the API surface the point's UUID, name and location for display [32].

```mermaid
---
title: "Cash point: from till to bill"
---
flowchart TD
  admin["Admin: Cash point config page"] --> rest["REST /billing/cashPoint"]
  rest --> service["CashPointService"]
  service --> dao["HibernateCashPointDAOImpl"]
  dao --> db["cashier_cash_point table"]
  order["Clinical order"] --> strategy["Order billing strategy"]
  checkin["O3 check-in form"] --> rest
  strategy --> resolve["resolveCashPoint"]
  resolve --> service
  strategy --> bill["Bill.cashPoint"]
  checkin --> bill
  bill --> receipts["Receipt numbering groups by CP"]
  timesheet["Timesheet: cashier shift"] --> service
```

The O3 documentation repository has no mention of cash points — a case-insensitive search for "cash point"/"cashPoint" across its markdown files returned nothing — so the rationale above is read from the code and in-code comments rather than a design document. I also only sampled the 1032 Java and 707 frontend matches: reports or dashboards that aggregate revenue by cash point, if any exist outside the files I read, were not examined.
</answer>
